title: Equations and variables
content: An equation states that two expressions have equal value. To solve for an unknown, apply inverse operations to both sides while preserving equality. Check a proposed solution by substituting it into the original equation.
cautions: Do the same operation to both sides; do not divide by zero.

title: Functions
content: A function assigns exactly one output to each allowed input. Domain is the set of allowed inputs; range is the set of outputs actually produced. A function can be represented by a rule, table, graph, or mapping.

title: Fractions and ratios
content: A fraction represents part-to-whole or a quotient. Ratios compare quantities. Equivalent fractions are formed by multiplying or dividing numerator and denominator by the same nonzero value. A percentage is a ratio per 100.

title: Exponents
content: For integer n>0, a^n means multiplying a by itself n times. Exponent rules include a^m·a^n=a^(m+n), (a^m)^n=a^(mn), and a^m/a^n=a^(m-n) when division is defined. Zero and negative exponents require nonzero base.
cautions: Avoid applying power rules across addition: (a+b)^n is generally not a^n+b^n.

title: Logarithms
content: A logarithm answers which exponent is needed: log_b(x)=y means b^y=x. For real logarithms, b>0, b≠1, and x>0. Logarithms convert multiplication into addition and can help solve exponential equations.

title: Linear systems
content: A system of equations seeks values satisfying all equations at once. Methods include substitution, elimination, and matrix methods. A system may have one solution, no solution, or infinitely many solutions.
cautions: Check the solution in every original equation.

title: Geometry: area and perimeter
content: Perimeter measures boundary length; area measures two-dimensional coverage. Rectangle area A=lw and perimeter P=2(l+w). Triangle area A=bh/2. Circle area A=πr² and circumference C=2πr.
cautions: Keep units: perimeter uses linear units; area uses square units.

title: Probability basics
content: Probability quantifies uncertainty from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain). For equally likely outcomes, P(event)=favorable outcomes/total outcomes. Complement rule: P(not A)=1−P(A). Independence means one event does not change the probability of another.
cautions: Do not assume outcomes are equally likely or independent without justification.

title: Scientific notation and units
content: Scientific notation writes a number as a×10^n with 1≤|a|<10. Unit conversions multiply by conversion factors equal to one, preserving quantity while changing units. Track units through calculations to catch mistakes.

title: Reasoning with graphs
content: Graphs reveal relationships and trends. For a straight line, slope m=(y2−y1)/(x2−x1) measures change in y per change in x. A graph shows association, but association alone does not prove causation.
cautions: Check axis scale, labels, units, and whether axes start at zero.
